A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeCCo study and support comparison of the text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. V3 retains Appendices A–H and adds Appendices I–J and a conference checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original model-fitting, posterior predictive, ablation, contamination, and synthetic model-recovery results using human behavioral and simulated data.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments using AIC-based feedback and LLM-generated prompt templates.

M1.justification: The core GeCCo pipeline is retained, but Appendices I–J introduce implemented variants that use AIC for feedback-model selection and obtain the prompt template from an LLM instead of handcrafting it.

E1.justification: The four human task domains, full- and partial-feedback learning conditions, and synthetic decision-making and learning tasks are retained. The added experiments vary pipeline configurations within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding literature baselines remain pWADD, RW4α, RW2α, Hybrid, and RL-WM. CENTAUR and the synthetic-task comparators are also retained; the new robustness figures reuse the relevant baseline and LLM backbone sets.

E3.justification: V3 adds AIC-based selection experiments for decision making and planning, and LLM-template controls for decision making and learning. Figures 13–14 report final performance using BIC. Previously stated splits, model configurations, temperatures, and fitting budgets are not revised.

E4.justification: Appendices I–J add targeted tests of dependence on the feedback selection criterion and handcrafted templates. Existing prompt ablations, noise tests, contamination checks, model recovery, and posterior predictive analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The five GeCCo runs, ten-run synthetic decision checks, SEM reporting, t-tests, mixed-effects analyses, and exceedance probabilities are retained. The new figures and checklist introduce no different uncertainty-estimation procedure or reported run count.

E6.justification: Original numerical results, including Table 1, are retained. Figures 13–14 add results reporting broadly comparable performance under the new pipeline variants, and Figure 5C corrects the high/low-load label assignment. The added experiments do not establish matched-setting performance gains over v2.

T1.justification: The cognitive-model definitions and update equations in the appendices are unchanged. Expanded explanations of BIC and exceedance probability introduce no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding summary retain the central claim that GeCCo generates interpretable cognitive models matching or outperforming literature baselines across four domains. The principal contributions and claims concerning CENTAUR remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 replaces direct neural-substrate mappings for the learning model with discussion of separate value traces and forgetting, and refines the planning and cognitive-load interpretations. It removes the participant-specific model-structure discussion and uses the new template experiment to qualify dependence on handcrafted templates.

D1.justification: V3 adds a GeCCo repository link and newly describes code parsing/execution, parameter-name extraction, and automatic restarting after generation failures. These are additional implementation disclosures, without establishing changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: The introduction explicitly connects GeCCo to Li et al. (2024a), already cited in v2. V3 adds Collins and Cockburn (2020), removes the generic cognitive-modeling overview, and drops four references associated with that overview and the removed neural-mechanism discussion.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the Methods, metric explanations, control-experiment prose, and Discussion. V3 organizes interpretations into Scientific Insight paragraphs, condenses related work and limitations, and adds acknowledgements and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 13–14, corrects the reversed high/low-load legend in Figure 5C, and relocates the main figures relative to their surrounding text. Front matter and captions receive limited formatting changes; the other existing graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new controls directly test dependence on BIC-based feedback and handcrafted templates, strengthening robustness evidence. Clearer implementation disclosures and the corrected Figure 5C legend improve reproducibility information and presentation accuracy. The central findings remain unchanged, and the new controls are only briefly documented, so the overall gain is limited.
